title: The Story of King Arthur and His Knights
author: Howard Pyle
openingText: Long ago there lived a very noble King named Uther-Pendragon, who became ruler over all of Britain. Two men gave him great help in winning the crown of the realm. One was a powerful enchanter and prophet whom people called Merlin the Wise, and he gave Uther-Pendragon very good advice. The other was an excellent and famous knight named Ulfius. Many people thought him the greatest war leader alive in those days, and he helped and advised Uther-Pendragon in battle. So, with the help of Merlin and Sir Ulfius, Uther-Pendragon defeated all his enemies and became King of the whole realm. After Uther-Pendragon had ruled for a number of years, he married a beautiful and gentle lady named Igraine. She was the widow of Gerlois, the Duke of Tintegal, and by him she had two daughters. One was named Margaise and the other Morgana le Fay, who was a famous sorceress. After the Queen married the mighty King, she brought her daughters to his Court. There Margaise was married to King Urien of Gore, and Morgana le Fay was married to King Lot of Orkney.
about:
Howard Pyle (1853–1911) wrote and illustrated this retelling of the Arthurian legend, published in 1903. It follows Arthur from the sword in the stone to the founding of the Round Table, then tells the stories of Merlin, Sir Pellias and Sir Gawaine.

Pyle drew on Malory and the older romances and told them in his own old-fashioned voice. This edition keeps the story, names and episodes, and renders the language in clear modern English.

whyItMatters.title: The legend that shaped English storytelling
whyItMatters.body: Arthur, Merlin, Excalibur, Guinevere and the Round Table appear in countless books and films. Pyle’s version is one of the clearest full tellings. Reading it shows where many familiar scenes come from.

whyItMatters.title: Honor tested in many small cases
whyItMatters.body: Knights keep or break vows, spare or kill enemies, and judge each other. The adventures keep asking what honor demands when it is inconvenient.

whyItMatters.title: A craftsman’s retelling
whyItMatters.body: Pyle chose and rearranged older stories into a connected tale. Comparing his choices with other Arthur books is a good way to see how legends are made.

angleCards.title: The women in the tales
angleCards.text: Watch Guinevere, the Lady of the Lake, Vivien and the damsels. What do they want and what do they do?
